sufficient in the urea sector. Total 6 new urea units have been set up under NIP-
2012 which includes 4 urea units set up through Joint Venture Companies (JVC) of
nominated PSUs and 2 urea units set up by the private companies. The units set
up through JVC are Ramagundam urea unit of Ramagundam Fertilizers and
Chemicals Ltd (RFCL) in Telangana and 3 urea units namely Gorakhpur, Sindri
and Barauni of Hindustan Urvarak & Rasayan Limited (HURL) at Gorakhpur in
Uttar Pradesh, Sindri in Jharkhand and Barauni in Bihar, respectively. The Barauni
unit has started Urea production on 18.10.2022 and has added urea production
capacity of 12.7 LMTPA.
Further, the Government of India is not directly involved in the setting up of
Nano Fertilizer Plants. Overall, 10 Nano Urea plants have been setup by PSUs and
other Fertilizer Companies across the country. The total production capacity of all
these Nano Urea plants presently in operation is 43.58 crore bottles (500 ml each)
per annum. Similarly, Fertilizer Companies have setup 3 Nano DAP plants with a
total production capacity of 7.64 crore bottles (500 ml each) per annum
across the country.
Also, a unit of M/s Indian Potash Limited manufactures SSP and is situated
at Muzaffarpur, Bihar.
The Government has implemented Nutrient Based Subsidy (NBS) Scheme
w.e.f. 01.04.2010 for Phosphatic and Potassic (P&K) Fertilizers. Under the
Scheme, P&K fertilizers are covered under Open General License (OGL) and
companies are free to import/manufacture these fertilizers as per their business

TRANSPORTATION OF GOODS THROUGH PORTS
5661. SHRI BAJRANG MANOHAR SONWANE:
Will the Minister of PORTS, SHIPPING AND WATERWAYS be pleased to state:

pages.original_text:
27.03.2026 719
(a) whether the Government is taking steps to promote transportation of goods
through ports and inland waterways in order to reduce logistics costs and
improve efficiency in the country, if so, the details thereof, State-wise;
(b) whether the Government has any proposal to strengthen port connectivity and
logistics infrastructure for facilitating export of agricultural and industrial
products;
(c) if so, the details thereof and the projects that have been proposed/under
implementation in Maharashtra particularly from the Marathwada region; and
(d) the manner in which the said initiatives are expected to benefit farmers,
industries and employment generation in the concerned regions?
THE MINISTER OF PORTS, SHIPPING AND WATERWAYS (SHRI
SARBANANDA SONOWAL):
(a) : The Government has taken various measures such as the construction of new
berths, terminals, parking plazas, mechanization/ modernization/ optimization of
existing berths and terminals, expansion of hinterland connectivity through rail and
road, elimination of manual Forms, facilitation of Direct Port Delivery and Entry,
installation of Container Scanners, e-delivery orders/ invoice/payments, RFID-
based gate automation system, fairway development, jetties, multi-modal terminals,
navigation improvements, policy incentives including a 35% subsidy for inland
transport, extension of tonnage tax to inland vessels, creation of cargo hubs,
operationalization of Indo-Bangladesh Protocol routes, etc. to reduce logistics costs
and improve the efficiency of major ports and inland waterways.

(b) to (d) : Sagarmala programme of the Government of India has a dedicated pillar
of port connectivity, which focuses on the last mile, and immediate hinterland
connectivity of the portsto minimize overall logistics costs. Further, Department for
Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT) has prepared a Comprehensive
Port Connectivity Plan (CPCP) in 2022 by reviewing connectivity of the operational
ports and identified the ports, which needed improvement of road and/ or rail
connectivity with nearby economic hubs. A total of 157 road connectivity projects
and 124 rail connectivity projects have been identified for implementation to
provide last mile port connectivity including in the state of Maharashtra where 2 rail
and 8 road port connectivity projects have been completed and 32 projects are
under various stages of implementation and planning. The details of these
connectivity projects are given in the enclosed Statement.
Improved road and rail connectivity between ports and their hinterland
enable farmers to access larger domestic and international markets, reduce
transportation time and costs, and minimize post-harvest losses, thereby
enhancing their incomes. Industries benefit from efficient movement of raw
materials and finished goods, leading to lower logistics costs, improved
competitiveness, and increased investment opportunities. Additionally, these
projects generate direct employment during construction and indirect employment
through growth in logistics, warehousing, and allied sectors, contributing to overall
regional economic development and livelihood enhancement.

PROMOTION OF YOGA AND NATUROPATHY SYSTEMS
5664. SHRI A. MANI:
Will the Minister of AYUSH be pleased to state:
(a) whether the National and International conferences and awareness
programmes are being organised every year to popularise and promote Yoga
and Naturopathy systems in the country in connection with the observance of
Naturopathy Day during the last six years and if so, the details thereof;
(b) whether any such conferences, workshops, public outreach programmes or
awareness campaigns have been conducted to encourage the adoption of
Yoga and Naturopathy among the public, students and healthcare
practitioners in the State of Tamil Nadu and if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether district-level events, training programmes or awareness activities
have been organized in rural or backward districts including the Dharmapuri
district as part of the efforts to popularize Yoga and Naturopathy practices and
if so, the details thereof;
(d) whether local Yoga institutions, naturopathy centres and AYUSH practitioners
from Dharmapuri district have been involved in such programmes and if so,
the details thereof; and
(e) the steps taken by the Government to further expand awareness and
participation in Yoga and Naturopathy systems in Tamil Nadu, particularly in
districts such as Dharmapuri?

including caesarean section. The entitlements include free drugs and
consumables, free diet during the stay, free diagnostics, free transportation
and free blood transfusion, if required. Similar entitlements are also in place
for sick infants.

o Extended PMSMA strategy focuses on quality antenatal care (ANC) for
pregnant women, especially high-risk pregnant (HRP) women and
individual HRP tracking with financial incentivization for the identified high-
risk pregnant women and accompanying Accredited Social Health
Activists (ASHAs) for extra 3 visits over and above the PMSMA visit.
o Surakshit Matritva Aashwasan (SUMAN) aims to provide assured,
dignified, respectful and quality healthcare at no cost and zero tolerance for
denial of services for every woman and newborn visiting a public health
facility, to end all preventable maternal and newborn deaths.
o Optimizing Postnatal Care aims to strengthen the quality of post-natal care
by laying emphasis on detection of danger signs in mothers and
incentivization of ASHAs for prompt detection, referral & treatment of such
high-risk postpartum mothers.
o The establishment of Special Newborn Care Units (SNCUs) and Newborn
Stabilization Units (NBSUs) under Facility Based Newborn Care (FBNC)
program to provide specialized care to sick and small newborns at district
and sub-district levels, addressing neonatal health complications.
o Village Health Sanitation and Nutrition Days (VHSNDs) are observed for
provision of maternal and child health services and creating awareness on
maternal and child care including nutrition in convergence with Ministry of
Women and Child Development.

(a) to (c) : Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR) has informed that ICMR-
National Institute of Epidemiology (NIE) conducted a study titled “Factors
associated with unexplained sudden deaths among adults aged 18-45 years in
India-A multicentric matched case-control study” at 47 tertiary care hospitals
located across 19 States/Union Territories of India during May-August 2023. Cases
were apparently healthy individuals without any known co-morbidity, who suddenly
(<24 hours of hospitalization or seen apparently healthy 24 hours before death)
died of unexplained causes during 1st October 2021-31st March 2023. Four
controls were included per case matched for age, gender and neighbourhood.
Information was collected regarding data on COVID-19 vaccination/infection, post-
COVID-19 conditions, family history of sudden death, smoking, recreational drug

pages.original_text:
27.03.2026 749
use, alcohol frequency, binge drinking and vigorous-intensity physical activity two
days before death among the cases / interviewed controls. A total of 729 sudden
death cases and 2916 controls were included in the analysis. It was observed that
receipt of any dose of COVID-19 vaccine reduced the odds for unexplained sudden
death. Receiving two doses of COVID-19 vaccine significantly reduced the odds of
unexplained sudden death. Past COVID-19 hospitalization, family history of sudden
death, binge drinking 48 hours before death/interview, use of recreational
drug/substance and performing vigorous-intensity physical activity 48 hours before
death/interview increased the odds of sudden death. Hence, the study observed
that COVID-19 vaccination did not increase the risk of unexplained sudden death
among young adults in India. Past COVID-19 hospitalization, family history of
sudden death and certain lifestyle behaviours increased the likelihood of
unexplained sudden death.
Further, in order to understand the reasons for heart attack, ICMR-National
Institute of Epidemiology (ICMR-NIE) conducted another multicentric matched
case-control study in 25 hospitals across India. Cases were patients aged 18-45
years admitted in the study hospitals with newly diagnosed Acute Myocardial
Infarction (AMI) between October 2021 and January 2023. Controls were patients
aged 18-45 years admitted in the same hospital for other causes, matched for time
of hospitalization. Information was collected regarding the various risk factors. The
study observed that hospitalization with AMI was associated with presence of any
known comorbidity, family history of thrombotic events and ever been smoker.

OPERATION OF MEDICAL STORES WITHOUT REGISTERED PHARMACISTS
5675. ADV. ADOOR PRAKASH:
Will the Minister of HEALTH AND FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) whether the Government has any proposal to allow medical stores to operate
without the mandatory presence of a registered pharmacist;
(b) if so, the details thereof and the reasons therefor;
(c) whether the Government has taken note of the concerns raised in reports
suggesting such as a move; and
(d) if so, the details thereof along with the response of the Government thereto?
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH AND FAMILY
WELFARE; AND MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CHEMICALS
AND FERTILIZERS (SHRIMATI ANUPRIYA PATEL):
(a) to (d) : Under the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940, and Rules thereunder the
license for Sale and Distribution of drugs are granted by the State Licensing
Authority appointed by the respective State Government. Licensee is required to
comply with all the conditions of license. State Licensing Authorities are
empowered to take action on violation of any conditions of such licenses. As per
the conditions of license, sales of Drugs shall be effected only by or under the
personal supervision of a registered pharmacist and no person can sale by retail
the Schedule H, H1 and X drugs without prescription of Registered Medical
Practitioner (RMP).

NUCLEIC ACID TESTING IN BLOOD BANKS
5679. SHRI DURAI VAIKO:
Will the Minister of HEALTH AND FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) whether the Government has taken note of the recent observations of the
Hon’ble Supreme Court regarding the feasibility of making Nucleic Acid
Testing (NAT) mandatory in blood banks to ensure safe blood transfusion, if
so, the details thereof;
(b) whether the Government proposes to introduce NAT screening for donated
blood in all Government and private blood banks across the Country, if so,
the details thereof, State-wise;
(c) the number of blood banks currently equipped with NAT facilities,
State-wise;
(d) whether the Government has assessed the cost implications and feasibility
of implementing NAT testing in all blood banks, particularly in Government
hospitals, if so, the details thereof;
(e) whether the Government maintains data on the number of persons affected
due to the transfusion of contaminated blood, including infections such as
HIV, Hepatitis B and Hepatitis C, during the last five years, year-wise; and
(f) the steps taken or proposed to be taken by the Government to strengthen
blood safety standards and prevent the transmission of infections through
blood transfusion?

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH AND FAMILY
WELFARE; AND MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CHEMICALS
AND FERTILIZERS (SHRIMATI ANUPRIYA PATEL):
(a) : In Writ Petition(s) (Civil) No(s). 184/2026, the Hon’ble Supreme Court
declined plea to make nucleic acid tests compulsory at blood banks, citing a lack
of specialized knowledge regarding medical protocols and the associated
economic impact on the state.
(b) to (d) : To prevent transfusion-transmitted infections, as per the National
Standards for Blood Banks and Blood Transfusion Services guidelines 2022, 4th
generation ELISA / Chemiluminescent Immunoassay (CLIA) is mandatory. The
Government does not propose to introduce mandatory NAT screening for
donated blood in all Government and private blood banks across the Country. At
present, out of 1131 blood centres supported by Dte.GHS, 349 are equipped with
NAT facilities. NAT is now available in prominent Institutes of National
Importance (INIs), Central Government hospitals, as well as in leading state
institutions.
(e) and (f): The data on the number of persons affected due to the transfusion of
contaminated blood, including infections such as HIV, Hepatitis B and Hepatitis
C, during the last five years is not maintained centrally. To strengthen blood
safety standards and prevent the transmission of infections through blood
transfusion, several guidelines have been issued from time to time.

assistance. Indian nationals can contact the Missions/Posts through various
channels like walk-in, email, social media, multilingual 24x7 emergency numbers
and also grievance redressal portals like MADAD, CPGRAMS, eMigrate etc. In
addition, Indian Missions/Posts abroad have established toll-free helplines,
Whatsapp numbers and have launched mobile apps to enable Indian
nationals contact concerned Indian Missions/Posts when in distress or in
emergency situations.

Health is a state subject. The primary responsibility of strengthening public
healthcare system, including filling up of the vacancies in healthcare facilities lies
with the respective State/UT Governments. The Ministry of Health and Family
Welfare provides technical and financial support to the States/UTs to strengthen
the public healthcare system in rural areas based on the proposals received in the
form of Programme Implementation Plans (PIPs) under National Health Mission.
Government of India provides approval for the proposal in the form of Record of
Proceedings (RoPs) as per norms & available resources. States/ UTs are to ensure
availability of HR by creating adequate number of regular posts as per the Indian
Public Health Standards (IPHS) in the long run and use NHM posts in the short to
medium term to fill critical gaps. The NHM supplements the regular human
resources by filling up the gaps in human resources in secondary and primary care
facilities (District Hospital and below) as per IPHS.
As per information provided by National Medical Commission (NMC), there
are 13,88,185 registered allopathic doctors and 7,51,768 registered AYUSH
practitioners. Assuming that 80% of registered practitioners in both the allopathic
and AYUSH systems are available, the doctor-population ratio in the country is
estimated to be 1:811.

practice in rural and remote areas of the country to address the shortage of doctors
in Community Health Centres and Primary Health Centres:

Government of India provides approval for the proposal in the form of Record of
Proceedings (RoPs) as per norms & available resources. States/ UTs are to ensure
availability of HR by creating adequate number of regular posts as per the Indian
Public Health Standards (IPHS) in the long run and use NHM posts in the short to
medium term to fill critical gaps. The NHM supplements the regular human
resources by filling up the gaps in human resources in secondary and primary care
facilities (District Hospital and below) as per IPHS.
As per information provided by National Medical Commission (NMC), there
are 13,88,185 registered allopathic doctors and 7,51,768 registered AYUSH
practitioners. Assuming that 80% of registered practitioners in both the allopathic
and AYUSH systems are available, the doctor-population ratio in the country is
estimated to be 1:811.
Under NHM, following types of incentives are given for encouraging doctors to
practice in rural and remote areas of the country to address the shortage of doctors
in Community Health Centres and Primary Health Centres:

pages.original_text:
27.03.2026 802
 Hard area allowance to specialist doctors for serving in rural and remote
areas and for their residential quarters so that they find it attractive to serve
in public health facilities in such areas.
 Honorarium to Gynecologists/ Emergency Obstetric Care (EmoC) trained,
Pediatricians & Anesthetist/ Life Saving Anaesthesia Skills (LSAS) trained
doctors is also provided to increase availability of specialists for conducting
Cesarean Sections in rural & remote area.
 Incentives like special incentives for doctors, incentive for Auxiliary Nurse
and Midwife (ANM) for ensuring timely Antenatal Checkup (ANC) checkup
and recording, incentives for conducting Adolescent Reproductive and
Sexual Health activities.
 States are also allowed to offer negotiable salary to attract specialist
including flexibility in strategies such as “You Quote We Pay”.
 Non-Monetary incentives such as preferential admission in post graduate
courses for staff serving in difficult areas and improving accommodation
arrangement in rural areas have also been introduced under NHM.
 Multi-skilling of doctors is supported under NHM to overcome the shortage of
specialists. Skill upgradation of existing HR is another major strategy under
NRHM for achieving improvement in health outcomes.
The measures/steps taken by the Government to increase the doctors/medical
professionals in the country include :-

State Government/Central Government Medical Colleges to increase
MBBS and PG seats.
 DNB qualification has been recognized for appointment as faculty to take
care of shortage of faculty.
 Enhancement of age limit for appointment/ extension/ re-employment
against posts of teachers/Dean/Principal/ Director in medical colleges upto
70 years.
 Family Adoption Programme (FAP): The FAP has been incorporated into
the MBBS curriculum to provide equitable healthcare access to rural
population. FAP involves medical colleges adopting villages and MBBS
students adopting families within these villages. This enables regular
follow-up of adopted families for vaccination, growth monitoring, menstrual
hygiene, Iron & Folic Acid (IFA) supplementation, healthy lifestyle practices,
nutrition, vector control, and medication adherence. It also helps in
educating families about ongoing government health programmes.
 District Residency Programme (DRP): The DRP notified by the NMC
provides for a compulsory three months posting cum training of PG medical

students at District Hospitals as a part of the course curriculum. DRP
benefits the public by strengthening healthcare delivery in rural and
underserved areas.

(a) to (d) : During the 15th Finance Commission cycle, 2 lakh Government owned

pages.original_text:

childhood care and development under Mission Saksham Anganwadi and Poshan
2.0. Saksham Anganwadis are equipped with better infrastructure than the
conventional Anganwadi Centres by providing LED screens, water
purifier/installation of RO Machine, Poshan Vatika, ECCE and BALA Paintings etc.
Prerequisites for an Anganwadi Centre to be considered for upgradation to
Saksham Anagnwadi Centre includes Government owned building, availability of
Electricity/power supply, drinking water facility, functional toilet and kitchen.
As on date, a total of 2 Lakh AWCs have been approved for upgradation as
Saksham AWCs including 23,697 AWCs to the State of Uttar Pradesh. The State
wise, district wise details of approved AWCs for upgradation to Saksham AWCs
including districts of Uttar Pradesh are given in the enclosed Statement.
Financial assistance of Rs. 1 Lakh per AWC with inter se flexibility amongst
the components on prescribed cost sharing basis is provided for the upgradation.
Under Mission Saksham Anganwadi and Poshan 2.0, an amount of Rs. 142.18
Crore has been allocated to the State of Uttar Pradesh for upgradation of AWCs as
Saksham Anganwadi Centres out of which an amount of Rs.117.22 Crore has
been released.

Ministry of Health and Family Welfare and CDSCO have taken following
measures to ease the regulatory landscape and fast-track approval for the
manufacturing of drugs in the country;
(i) On 25.02.2026, CDSCO has issued a Guidance Document for
submission of application for obtaining Manufacturing License by the
Applicant based on Dossier based licensing of Drugs. The dossier based
approval process promotes the transparency and ensures fairness in the
decision making process. The dossier based approach is more efficient
than the individual evaluation as it streamlines the process and reduces
the need for redundant assessment.
(ii) On 23.02.2026, CDSCO issued a circular to fast-track approvals for new
drugs by allowing No-Objection Certificates (NOCs) for laboratory testing
to be issued immediately upon receipt of applications a step aimed at
reducing delays in the drug approval process. Under the revised
procedure, NoCs for testing new drugs at designated government
laboratories shall be granted upfront, instead of waiting for prior scrutiny
of detailed technical specifications.

(a) whether the Union Government has taken serious note on the fact that large
number of Indian aspirants have been suffering because of the stringent
measures taken by USA to issue of H1B Visa, if so, the details thereof;
(b) the steps taken by the Union Government to take a strong and coordinated

pages.original_text:

effort to find a permanent amicable solution to solve the H1B Visa issues; and
(c) whether the Government taken any steps regarding the unprecedented
hardship faced by Indian students and workers in USA, Canada, UK and
Middle East countries, if so, the details thereof?
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST
AND CLIMATE CHANGE; AND MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF
EXTERNAL AFFAIRS (SHRI KIRTI VARDHAN SINGH):
(a) to (c) : The Government is aware of the H-1B visa-related challenges faced by
Indian nationals. Visa-related policies and associated decisions are sovereign
matters. The U.S. Government’s stated position is that every visa adjudication is a
national security decision and that a U.S. visa is a privilege and not a right.
In December 2025, the U.S. Department of State announced vetting of the
online presence of all H-1B applicants and their dependents (H-4) to determine
their admissibility to the United States. Subsequently, the consular appointments of
several H-1B and H-4 visa applicants scheduled in December 2025 were
rescheduled to new dates in 2026, leading to a large number of the applicants
remaining in India.
India believes that skilled talent mobility has long played a significant role in
promoting technology advancement, innovation, economic growth, and wealth
creation in both India and the United States. Stakeholders in both countries remain
engaged for facilitating continued support for legal mobility.

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST
AND CLIMATE CHANGE; AND MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF
EXTERNAL AFFAIRS (SHRI KIRTI VARDHAN SINGH):
(a) to (c) : The U.S. Government, through the Department of State’s public
notifications dated 18th June and 3rd December 2025, respectively, expanded its
screening and vetting procedures which required H-1B visa applicants and their
dependents (H-4) to adjust the privacy settings of their social media
profiles to “public.”
The U.S. Government’s stated position is that every visa adjudication is a
national security decision and that a U.S. visa is a privilege and not a right. The

objective of the recent notifications was said to be to curb visa abuses, protect the
American worker, and to identify visa applicants who may be inadmissible to the
United States. Subsequently, the consular appointments of several H-1B and H-4
visa applicants scheduled in December 2025 were rescheduled to new dates in
2026, resulting in many applicants remaining in India.
The H-1B visa programme is governed by U.S. laws and procedures, and
the issuance of such visas is subject to due processes carried out by the
competent U.S. authorities – the U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services
(USCIS) for visa adjudications within the United States or the relevant U.S.
Embassy / Consulate for visa adjudications overseas. The relatively high number of
Indian nationals in the H-1B visa programme reflects the demand-driven nature of
the U.S. labour market, particularly in high-skill sectors such as technology and
engineering, and the availability of a large pool of qualified Indian professionals.
Government of India remains engaged with the U.S. Government to
promote mutually advantageous and secure frameworks that allow for streamlining
avenues for legal mobility of students and professionals and facilitating short-term
tourist and business travel.

self-reliant the following measures have been taken by the Government:
(i) D/o Fertilizers has issued guidelines 18.01.2024 to ensure
reasonableness of MRP and encourage domestic production.
(ii) Based on the requests, the new manufacturing units or increase in
manufacturing capacity of existing units have been recognized / taken on
record under the NBS Scheme.
(iii) The number of P&K fertilizers covered under NBS policy has increased
from 22 grades in 2021 to 28 grades.

fertilizer, has been approved since Kharif, 2022 to promote SSP usage
for providing Phosphatic or 'P' nutrient to the soil.

examination.

Scheme (CSS) for ‘Establishment of new medical colleges attached with existing
district/referral hospitals’ with preference to underserved areas and aspirational
districts, where there is no existing Government or private medical college. A total
of 157 Medical Colleges have been approved in the various districts across the
country out of which 137 are already functional. Further, support has also been

practice. Accordingly, regulation namely, the National Commission for Indian

(d) : The statutory provision under the National Commission for Indian System of
Medicine Act, 2020 and the National Commission for Homoeopathy Act, 2020
ensures regulation and protection of duly registered practitioners including the
Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribes dominated areas.
(e) : A statutory mechanism exists under the National Commission for Indian
System of Medicine Act, 2020 and the National Commission for Homoeopathy Act,
2020. Section 31 of the NCISM Act, 2020 and NCH Act, 2020 provides for
regulation of professional or ethical misconduct, under which the State Medical
Council and Board of Ethics and Registration, where State Medical Council is not
established, are empowered to consider matters relating to professional
misconduct and grievances of practitioners. In addition, grievances can be
addressed through existing platforms such as the Centralized Public Grievance
Redress and Monitoring System (CPGRAM) and through concerned State/UT
authorities and respective Commissions.

(e) : NMPB has adopted a multi-pronged approach to ensure that medicinal plant
cultivation and collection in ecologically sensitive areas remain sustainable and
biodiversity-friendly. Key safeguards include promoting cultivation over wild
collection, sustainable harvesting guidelines, establishing herbal gardens and
supporting community-based conservation initiatives.
1. Encouraged the farmers for cultivation of medicinal plants instead of relying
on wild collection, reducing pressure on forests.
2. Published booklets and manuals on sustainable harvesting methods to
prevent overexploitation along with the training programs for collectors and
local communities on non-destructive harvesting techniques (e.g., selective
pruning, seasonal collection).
3. Community and Institutional Involvement-Works with local communities,
Village Forest Committee (VFC), Biodiversity Management Committee
(BMC) members, Non-Government Organisations (NGOs) and forest
departments to integrate conservation with livelihoods.
4. Establishment of Herbal Gardens.

To strengthen the drug testing infrastructure and enhance laboratory
capacity across the country, Ministry of Health and Family Welfare has
implemented a Centrally Sponsored Scheme 'Strengthening of States’ Drug
Regulatory System (SSDRS). The scheme envisages upgrading existing State
laboratories, setting up of new drug testing laboratories and upgradation of existing
State drug control offices in the country. Under the SSDRS Scheme, funds totalling
Rs. 756 Crore has been released to States/UTs as part of the Central Share and
19 New Drug Testing Labs have been constructed and 28 existing labs have been
up-graded in various States/UTs. Further, Section 26 of the Drugs and Cosmetics
Act, 1940, specifically empowers individual citizens and consumer associations to
have medicines tested.
The Drugs Rules, 1945 have been amended in year 2023 to mandate that
manufacturers of the top 300 drug formulation brands listed in Schedule H2 shall
print or affix a Bar Code or QR Code on the primary packaging label, or on the
secondary label where space is insufficient, to store data readable through
software applications for authentication. Similarly, the Rules have also been
amended to require that every Active Pharmaceutical Ingredient (bulk drug),
whether manufactured or imported, shall bear a QR Code on each level of
packaging containing data readable through software applications to facilitate
tracking and tracing.

OUT-OF-POCKET EXPENDITURE ON HEALTH IN KERALA
5712. SHRI SHAFI PARAMBIL:
Will the Minister of HEALTH AND FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) the percentage and per capita Out-Of-Pocket Expenditure (OOPE) on health
in the State of Kerala during the last ten years, year-wise;
(b) the comparative data on out-of-pocket health expenditure in other States and
Union Territories during the same period;
(c) whether Kerala’s OOPE is higher or lower than the national average and if so,
the reasons thereof;
(d) the major components contributing to out-of-pocket expenditure in Kerala
including medicines, diagnostics, hospitalization and outpatient care; and
(e) the steps taken by the Union Government to reduce the financial burden on
households, including the expansion of Ayushman Bharat and other health
insurance schemes in the said State?

WELFARE; AND MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CHEMICALS
AND FERTILIZERS (SHRIMATI ANUPRIYA PATEL):
(a) to (c) : As per latest available National Health Accounts estimates, the per
capita Out-Of-Pocket Expenditure (OOPE) and OOPE share in Total Health
Expenditure (THE) for States, including Kerala, for FY 2014-15 to FY 2021-22 is
given in the enclosed Statement.

Ayushman Bharat Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (AB-PMJAY) aims
to provide health cover of Rs. 5 lakhs per family per year for secondary and tertiary
care hospitalization to more than 12 crore families constituting the economically
vulnerable bottom 40% of India’s population. States/UTs implementing AB-PMJAY
have further expanded the beneficiary base, at their own cost. Additionally, the
scheme has been expanded to cover 6 crore senior citizens of age 70 years and
above belonging to 4.5 crore families irrespective of their socio-economic status
under AB-PMJAY with Vay Vandana Card. As on 28th February 2026, a total of
11.69 crore hospital admissions amounting to Rs. 1.73 lakh crore have been
authorized under the scheme since its launch in September 2018, including 78.35
lakh hospital admissions amounting to Rs. 9,525.17 crore in Kerala.
Besides, quality generic medicines are made available at affordable
prices to all under Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Pariyojana (PMBJP) in
collaboration with the State Governments. Affordable Medicines and Reliable
Implants for Treatment (AMRIT) Pharmacy stores have been set up in some
hospitals/institutions.

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF WOMEN AND CHILD
DEVELOPMENT (SHRIMATI SAVITRI THAKUR):
(a) to (e) : The One Stop Centre (OSC) is a component of the Sambal vertical
under the Mission Shakti. It provides integrated support and assistance under one
roof to women affected by violence and those in distress, both in private and public
spaces. It provides services like medical aid, legal aid and advice, temporary
shelter, police assistance and psycho-social counselling to needy women. As on
date, 926 One Stop Centres have been made operational across the country out of
which, 42 One Stop Centres are operational in Chhattisgarh.
As per the Mission Shakti guidelines, the Central Government provides
100% financial assistance to States/ UTs for appointment/hiring 13 manpower
resources including 1 Psycho-social Counsellor, 1 Para Legal Personnel/ Lawyer
and 1 Para Medical Personnel at each OSC. The overall implementation of the
OSC scheme lies with the State Governments and UT Administrations.
Further, once in a year, the Programme Approval Board (PAB) monitors with
States and UTs, the progress of activities under the scheme and reviews status of
achievement of objectives and effective delivery of services to women and children.
Apart from this, officials of the Ministry continuously review the scheme through
meetings, video conferencing and by making field visits to States and UTs from
time to time.

technical and financial support to the States/UTs for emergency medical services
through functional National Ambulance Service (NAS) network which is linked with
a centralized toll-free number 108/102. Dial 108 is primarily designed to attend to
patients of critical care, trauma and accident victims etc. Dial 102 services includes
basic patient transport that aims to cater to the needs of pregnant women and
children and others too. Apart from this, 112 is India’s pan-India single emergency
number under the Emergency Response Support System (ERSS) of Government
of India, integrating police, fire, and ambulance services (including NHM 102/108
services).
As per NHM norms, one Basic Life Support (BLS) ambulance per 100,000
population and one Advance Life Support (ALS) ambulance per 500,000 population
is provided. The National Ambulance Code (AIS-125) sets technical and safety
norms. The model for implementation of NAS is chosen by respective State/UT
Government, depending upon their requirement and suitability. States/UTs have
been given this flexibility to propose for a particular type of ambulance and the
required number of ambulances including the operational costs based on the
requirement and the gap analysis in their respective State Programme
Implementation Plan (PIP). States/UTs also have the flexibility to deploy the
ambulances based on need/service requirements, taking into account the needs of
the citizens, including those living in rural or remote areas. Some States use bike
and boat ambulances in remote areas. Total 83 ALS, 306 BLS and 944 others are

Following measures are taken by the Government every season for
ensuring timely and adequate supply of fertilizers in the country, including the
State of Odisha:
i. Before the commencement of each cropping season, Department of
Agriculture and Farmers Welfare (DA&FW), in consultation with all the
State Governments, assesses the State-wise & month-wise
requirement of fertilizers.
ii. On the basis of requirement projected by DA&FW, D/o Fertilizers
allocates adequate quantities of fertilizers to States by issuing monthly
supply plan and continuously monitors the availability.
iii. movement of all major subsidized fertilizers is monitored throughout the
country by an on-line web based monitoring system called integrated
Fertilizer Management System (iFMS).
iv. Regular Weekly Video Conference is conducted jointly by DA&FW and
D/o Fertilizers with State Agriculture Officials and corrective actions are
taken to dispatch fertilizers as indicated by the State Governments.

administrative measures, in consultation with stakeholders and in compliance
with judicial directions, to ensure the independence, functional autonomy and
effective functioning of tribunals.

(DMHP) component of the NMHP has been sanctioned for implementation in
767 districts for which support is provided to States/UTs through the National
Health Mission. Facilities made available under DMHP at the Community
Health Centre (CHC) and Primary Health Centre (PHC) levels, include
outpatient services, assessment, counselling/ psycho-social interventions,
continuing care and support to persons with severe mental disorders, drugs,
outreach services, ambulance services etc. In addition to above services there
is a provision of 10 bedded in-patient facility at the District level.
The Government is also taking steps to integrate mental healthcare
services at primary healthcare level. The Government has upgraded more than
1.77 lakh Sub Health Centres (SHCs) and Primary Health Centres (PHCs) to
Ayushman Arogya Mandirs. Mental health services have been added in the
packages of services under Comprehensive Primary Health Care provided at
these Ayushman Arogya Mandirs. Operational guidelines and training manuals
for various cadres on Mental, Neurological, and Substance Use Disorders
(MNS) at Ayushman Arogya Mandirs have been released under the ambit of
Ayushman Bharat.
Under the tertiary care component of NMHP, 25 Centres of
Excellence have been sanctioned to increase the intake of students in PG
departments in mental health specialties as well as to provide tertiary level
treatment facilities. Further, the Government has also supported 19
Government medical colleges/institutions to strengthen 47 PG Departments in
mental health Specialties.

these Ayushman Arogya Mandirs. Operational guidelines and training manuals
for various cadres on Mental, Neurological, and Substance Use Disorders
(MNS) at Ayushman Arogya Mandirs have been released under the ambit of
Ayushman Bharat.
Under the tertiary care component of NMHP, 25 Centres of
Excellence have been sanctioned to increase the intake of students in PG
departments in mental health specialties as well as to provide tertiary level
treatment facilities. Further, the Government has also supported 19
Government medical colleges/institutions to strengthen 47 PG Departments in
mental health Specialties.

of the District Mental Health Programme to provide universal access to
equitable, accessible, affordable and quality mental health care through 24 x 7
tele-mental health counselling services. For this, a toll-free number (14416)
has been set up across the country.
As on 03.03.2026, 36 States/ UTs have set up 53 Tele MANAS Cells.

by States. More than 34.34 lakh calls have been handled on the helpline
number since inception.

Mobile Application is a comprehensive mobile platform that has been
developed to provide support for mental health issues ranging from well being

facility under Tele-MANAS, as another upgrade to the already existing audio
calling facility.

UNAVAILABILITY OF FERTILIZERS
5728. SHRI ABU TAHER KHAN:
Will the Minister of CHEMICALS AND FERTILIZERS be pleased to state:
(a) whether the Government is aware of the plight and protest of the farmer
for the unavailability of fertilizers, if so, the details thereof;
(b) the initiatives taken by the Government to ensure that there are adequate
levels of fertilizers in the country; and
(c) whether there has been a loss of acreage of crop sowing due to
unavailability of fertilizers, if so, the details thereof?
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH AND FAMILY
WELFARE; AND MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CHEMICALS
AND FERTILIZERS (SHRIMATI ANUPRIYA PATEL):
(a) to (c) : The following steps are taken by the Government every season for
ensuring timely and adequate availability of fertilizers in the country:
(i) Before the commencement of each cropping season, Department of
Agriculture and Farmers Welfare (DA&FW), in consultation with all the
State Governments, assesses the State-wise & month-wise
requirement of fertilizers.
(ii) On the basis of requirement projected by DA&FW, D/o Fertilizers
allocates adequate quantities of fertilizers to States by issuing monthly
supply plan and continuously monitors the availability.

ensuring timely and adequate availability of fertilizers in the country:

REDUCTION OF CANCER DRUG PRICES
5729. SHRI RAJMOHAN UNNITHAN:
Will the Minister of HEALTH AND FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) whether the recent reduction in prices of selected cancer drugs has
significantly improved affordability for patients across States, if so, the
details thereof, State-wise;
(b) whether public hospitals in Kerala have reported increased access to
essential oncology medicines, if so, the details thereof; and
(c) the steps taken or proposed to be taken by the Government to ensure the
sustained affordability of life-saving drugs and equitable access to
specialised treatment?
THE MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF AYUSH; AND MINISTER
OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH AND FAMILY WELFARE (SHRI
PRATAPRAO GANPATRAO JADHAV):
(a) : The reduction in prices of selected anti-cancer drugs has contributed to
improved affordability for patients, as measures such as trade margin
rationalisation and price fixation by NPPA have led to reduction of prices of
several drugs, thereby lowering out-of-pocket expenditure and increasing
access to essential oncology medicines across States. further, reduction in
customs duty and GST on certain high-cost cancer drugs has resulted in
corresponding decrease in their market prices, enabling more patients to avail
treatment, though State-wise quantification of such improvement is not
centrally maintained.

(b) : The State Government of Kerala has informed that the procurement of
oncology drugs in the public health hospitals in Kerala is through Kerala
Medical Services Cooperation and the costly medicines are distributed through
Karunya outlets which are the off-shoots of Kerala Medical Services

under NLEM, 2022 has resulted in reduction of around 21% from the
ceiling prices fixed under NLEM, 2015, leading to annual savings of
around ₹294.34 crore to patients.

which is the primary legislation for ensuring safety, security, dignity and well-
being of children and is implemented by the States and UTs. The Act creates
statutory structures at the State and District levels which include State Child
Protection Society, Child Welfare Committees, Juvenile Justice Boards (JJBs),
District Child Protection Units. It also provides for establishment of Child Care
Institutions (CCIs).

Committees (CWCs) have been empowered to take decisions with regard to
the children in need of care and protection, keeping their best interest in mind.

District Child Protection Units. It also provides for establishment of Child Care
Institutions (CCIs).

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH AND FAMILY
WELFARE; AND MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CHEMICALS
AND FERTILIZERS (SHRIMATI ANUPRIYA PATEL):
(a) : Integrated Fertilizer Management System (iFMS) was launched in June
2016 which is a comprehensive, all-integrated system covering all
functionalities in the fertilizer supply chain. This comprehensive system covers
the entire supply chain, meticulously capturing transactional data from raw
material procurement, imports to fertilizer production and transportation via rail
or road from plants, rake houses, ports to district warehouses, and finally sale
at PoS enabled retailers, everything aligned with monthly supply plans at
district level and the movement of fertilizers is being captured in real time. In
order to prevent diversion and thereby ensure affordable and uninterrupted
fertilizer availability to farmers, Department of Fertilizers has put a ceiling of 50
bags of subsidized fertilizers per buyer per month i.e. 300 bags of subsidized
fertilizers per season. Additionally, a monthly list of 'Top 20 buyers' of each
district is made available in the iFMS log-in of respective district magistrates for
taking necessary action at their end.
Besides, Department of Fertilizers has also developed a dashboard
which can be accessed by authorized users at https://ur. The dashboard is
developed to facilitate easy monitoring by various Stake holders viz. State
Agriculture Departments, District Collectors and State Marketing Federations.
The State Governments are also monitoring the availability and supply of
fertilizers through iFMS and e-Urvarak Dashboard portals.

the fertilizer companies through the existing retailer margin of Rs 50 per MT
being given by the Government of India.

complaints received at Department of Fertilizers level regarding these
malpractices is sent to concerned State Government to take appropriate action
under Essential Commodities Act, 1955 and Fertilizer Control Order, 1985.

persons involved in said malpractices, as per provisions of EC Act. Any
complaints received at Department of Fertilizers level regarding these
malpractices is sent to concerned State Government to take appropriate action
under Essential Commodities Act, 1955 and Fertilizer Control Order, 1985.

been reported in Hingoli district.

IMPACT ON HEALTH DUE TO AIR POLLUTION
5746. SHRI GOVIND MAKTHAPPA KARJOL:
Will the Minister of HEALTH AND FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) the details of increasing levels of air pollution levels in various parts of the
country and their impact on public health, particularly on lung infections
and respiratory diseases, State/UT- wise;
(b) whether the Government has conducted any study to assess the link
between rising air pollution levels and increasing hospital admissions and
mortality due to respiratory and cardiovascular diseases and if so, the
details thereof; and
(c) the preventive measures taken or being taken by the Government and the
public health advisories issued to protect vulnerable groups including
children, the elderly and persons with pre-existing respiratory conditions?
THE MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF AYUSH; AND MINISTER
OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH AND FAMILY WELFARE (SHRI
PRATAPRAO GANPATRAO JADHAV):
(a) : Air pollution is one of the factors affecting respiratory ailments and
associated diseases. Health is impacted by several factors, including food
habits, occupational habits, socio- economic status, medical history, immunity,
heredity, etc., of the individuals including children apart from the environment.
Details of the air pollution levels in the various cities of India may be seen at
https://cpcb.nic.in/AQI_Bulletin.php.

to State/UTs suggesting ways to reduce the impact of air pollution.

(d) : Nipah virus disease is an emerging zoonotic infectious disease caused by
the Nipah virus (NiV) that mainly affects pigs and humans. Human infections
usually occur in clusters or outbreaks, particularly among close contacts and
caregivers of infected individuals. The natural reservoir host of the virus is
believed to be Pteropus fruit bats (flying foxes).
According to the information available fruit bats play a significant role in
the transmission of the virus. Human infections may occur due to spillover of
the virus from fruit bats to intermediate hosts or directly to humans. In India,
outbreaks have been associated with exposure to contaminated food sources
and close contact with infected individuals, which may lead to periodic
occurrence of cases in certain geographical areas.

under the Pradhan Mantri Ayushman Bharat Health Infrastructure Mission

progress reports submitted by the States/UTs. The progress under the Mission

Arogya Mandirs (AAMs), establishment of Integrated Public Health
Laboratories (IPHLs), and Critical Care Blocks (CCBs) at district hospitals. The
States/UTs have reported progress in the operationalization and upgradation
of these health infrastructure components in accordance with the approved
proposals and timelines under PM-ABHIM, and the same is being regularly
reviewed by the Ministry to ensure effective implementation of the Mission.

is carried out through a robust, multi-layered framework that includes review of
State-wise Key Deliverables against approved targets during NPCC meetings
with all States/UTs including Andhra Pradesh, regular assessment of
performance through the Output–Outcome Monitoring Framework (OOMF). In
addition, annual Common Review Missions (CRMs) provide independent, on-
ground assessments of programme implementation, health system
strengthening, and progress on key indicators, enabling identification of gaps,
course correction, and strengthening of accountability at State and
District levels.

(ii) Need to promote Fisheries by utilizing the potential water resources of
Govind Sagar and Maharana Pratap Sagar reservoirs in Hamirpur
Parliamentary Constituency, Himachal Pradesh
SHRI ANURAG SINGH THAKUR (HAMIRPUR): Hamirpur Parliamentary
Constituency is uniquely flanked by two of India’s largest manmade reservoirs,
Gobind Sagar (Bhakra Dam), Maharana Pratap Sagar (Pong Dam). Together
they spread across nearly 42,000 hectares of water surface, offering vast,
promising resource that perfectly aligns with Government’s vision of Blue
Revolution and sustainable fisheries growth. Building on progressive policies
already in place, the communities living around these reservoirs can achieve
far greater prosperity. Fish production in Himachal Pradesh can be given
steady advancement by using productivity potential of these two reservoirs,
fully harnessing it to create new opportunities, enhance incomes and
strengthen local livelihoods through modern interventions. In keeping with the
Government’s commitment to fisher welfare, a dedicated time-bound
comprehensive aquaculture development plan is needed, specifically for
Gobind Sagar and Maharana Pratap Sagar. This should include modern fish
landing centres, ice plants, trout and carp hatcheries, cage culture expansion,
direct marketing linkages, along with funding under the Blue Revolution
Scheme for infrastructure, fingerling stocking and fisher welfare, along with
focused projects by the National Fisheries Development Board covering
raceway units, fish seed production, post-harvest facilities and skill
development for local communities. These steps would transform the lives of
people in districts of Una, Hamirpur, Bilaspur, Kangra.

requirements. Globally, this shift is already underway. Facing similar capacity
crunches, Japan and Argentina recently raised their pilot retirement ages to 68
years, and countries like Australia, New Zealand, and Canada have abolished
maximum age limits entirely for domestic operations. They prioritize rigorous
bi-annual medical, cognitive, and simulator assessments over an arbitrary
chronological number. While a First Officer can be trained relatively quickly,
developing a Captain requires thousands of flight hours. Raising the retirement
age keeps experienced pilots in command longer, giving younger pilots more
time to safely upgrade. Economically, this extension also drastically reduces
Indian airlines' reliance on expensive foreign expatriate pilots. Hence, I urge
the adoption of a similar health-based extension framework so that we can
meet growing passenger demand and maintain regional connectivity, while
ensuring absolute passenger safety and cost-effectiveness.

SHRI HAMDULLAH SAYEED (LAKSHADWEEP): I would like to draw the
attention of the Government to the grave difficulties confronting Lakshadweep
residents due to the Lakshadweep Administration's order of 14th March 2026,
which cancels all diversion certificates for construction on private and
Pandaram lands across the islands. Sir, these certificates, issued after due
verification by competent authorities, enabled families to build homes on their
land. Many have invested life savings in good faith, constructing or expanding
houses over the years. This abrupt cancellation has sown widespread
uncertainty and distress. Ongoing constructions face stop memos, stranding
households mid-project. Families who borrowed or pooled resources now

endure severe financial and social hardships. Lakshadweep's scarce land and
traditional holdings—private plots and community-used Pandaram lands—

devise a practical, resident-friendly mechanism to shield those who acted in
good faith from penalties. The Union Government must provide immediate
relief to affected households in Lakshadweep.

(xvii) Need to set up a sub-centre of an Agricultural University along with
implementation of various projects under Agricultural Schemes in
Ahilyanagar district, Maharashtra
SHRI NILESH DNYANDEV LANKE (AHMEDNAGAR): I wish to draw the
attention of the Government regarding the farmers in my Parliamentary
Constituency—specifically those residing in the talukas of Nagar, Karjat,
Jamkhed, Shrigonda, Parner, Pathardi, and Shevgaon within the Ahilyanagar
(Ahmednagar) district—who are primarily dependent on summer irrigation and
dryland farming. Considering the prevailing climatic conditions, soil texture,
and the persistent drought-like situation in this region, it is absolutely essential
to establish a sub-center of an Agricultural University that can provide farmers
with research support and modern technology at the local level. Such a sub-
center would enable farmers to access up-to-date information, new
technologies, and remedial measures right within their own locality. Methods
for achieving higher yields with minimal water usage would be developed,
thereby boosting farmers' incomes and improving their economic well-being.
Furthermore, it would open up new avenues for the local rural youth to engage
in agricultural research. Ahilyanagar is a district possessing immense potential
for progress across the sectors of youth empowerment, agriculture, and
education. However, the implementation of several crucial projects has been

our personal attention to this critical issue. Furthermore, the Comptroller and
Auditor General (CAG) report regarding the railways has also recently been
released. Regrettably, due to increased operational speeds, we are currently

tragic coincidence, today marks exactly two months since the passing of my
brother; he lost his life in a plane crash on January 28th. When the patriarch-
the primary provider of a family is lost, the grief and devastation inflicted upon
that family are immense. It is for this very reason that safety-whether in the air,
on the rails, or on the roads-is absolutely essential. It has been two months
since my brother's plane crash occurred, yet we have still not received justice.
My brother served as the Deputy Chief Minister of Maharashtra; if even he
cannot obtain justice, how can the common person ever hope to receive it? My
elder brother's son, Rohit, has reached out to various political parties for
support. Shri Arvind Ji is present here today, as are representatives from the
DMK, the SP, and various other parties. I do not wish to politicize this issue;
however, Rohit Pawar made tireless efforts to have an FIR (First Information

state proved futile, he appealed to authorities in several other states, pleading
with them to take cognizance of the matter and ensure that justice is served to
Ajit Pawar. If the Deputy Chief Minister of a state meets with an accident and
an FIR is not even registered, where are the common citizens supposed to tum

Maharashtra. With folded hands, I appeal to both the Government of

Furthermore, due to the war-like situation in West Asia and the Red Sea crisis,
our exports have completely collapsed, and shipping costs have skyrocketed
by 200% to 300%. Similarly, cotton, soybean, and maize farmers in Dhule and
Jalgaon are in deep distress as prices have fallen below the actual cost of
production. The grape growers of Nashik and the banana farmers of Jalgaon
are fighting a battle on two fronts: global conflict and climate change. The
unseasonal rain and hailstorms in January and February 2026 have already
damaged crops over more than 50,000 hectares of land.
Madam, through you, I urge the Government to take an immediate and
decisive action. A guaranteed legal MSP must be provided for onions, and the
government should provide a 50% direct subsidy on transport to compensate
for the surge in freight costs caused by global tensions. Furthermore, the
number of NAFED and CCI procurement centers in Dhule and North
Maharashtra must be increased to ensure 100% procurement of cotton,
soybean, and maize at MSP. Additionally, a special financial package should
be announced for the farmers of North Maharashtra who have suffered heavy
losses due to these unseasonal rains and global market fluctuations.
Madam, if the Government does not intervene immediately, the rural
economy of North Maharashtra will be completely devastated. I earnestly
request the government, through this House, to rescue our Annadata from this
dire crisis and provide them with the justice they deserve.
Thank you.

downtrodden people are very much affected. Moreover, this is the season for
marriages in Tamil Nadu. Auspicious days are also listed in this month for such
occasions. People belonging to poor farming families, with their lifelong

should immediately intervene in such matters and refund all those money to
those from whom it was collected. Following such a strict procedure adds to
the difficulties faced in today's world. Therefore, I urge that an Amendment be
brought in Election Code of Conduct or the Election related Laws which is the
need of the hour.

seized money? He was Mr Nainar Nagendran the BJP candidate. It remains
unclear as to what happened to that huge money that was seized from such a
highly placed person. But the poor people are affected day in and day out.

*SHRIMATI MALVIKA DEVI (KALAHANDI): Thank you, Chairperson Ma'am,
for giving me the opportunity to speak. I want to ask about an important matter
today. Nuapada comes under Kalahandi loksabha constituency. The
Sunabeda Tiger Reserve is located there. We have received in principle
approval for upgradation in this regard. Tiger reserve has been permitted in
Sunabeda by National Tiger Conservation Authority. And we need actual
upgradation and notification for this Tiger reserve. It spreads in an area around
600 square kilo meters. It is situated between Odisha and Chhatishgarh. If we
get a Tiger reserve here then migrant labour issue would be resolved, It would
boost tourism sector as well as the economy of the state. Hence I request the
concerned Minister through you Ma'am, to declare this as a Tiger reserve as
soon as possible. Thank you.
DR. KADIYAM KAVYA (WARANGAL): Thank you, Chairperson Madam. I hail
the women power for giving all the women MPs first priority to speak their word
during the ‘Zero Hour’.

Paraquat Dichloride is an internationally recognised and most acutely
toxic herbicide used in agriculture. Even a minimum exposure of that either
through ingestion, inhalation or skin contact can cause hazardous effects on
human body including lung, kidney and liver failure, and finally death.
The sad thing here is that there is no antidote for this dangerous poison
which is frequently used by the poor farmers. It is also causing harm to the
land, water and soil. Nearly 70 countries, including China, UK and others, have
banned this drug.
I would request the hon. Agriculture Minister, and Chemical and
Fertilizers Minister to please ban this dangerous drug because there is no
coming back, and whoever is consuming this is finally dying due to it. As the
States have no power to permanently ban this drug, I would request the
Central Government to make a policy and ban Paraquat Dichloride. Thank you
so much.

On 7 February 2026, an electric swing at the Surajkund International
Crafts Mela in Haryana collapsed, killing a police inspector and injuring several
others. Similar risks exist in ziplines, bungee platforms, scuba boats and ATV
trails, where permissions are ad hoc and inspections are sporadic.
The Ministry of Tourism's Indian Adventure Tourism Guidelines, 2018 list
minimum standards, but they are not a statutory enforcement mechanism.
Madam, through you, I urge the Union Government to create a single statutory
National Authority for Adventure Sports and Amusement Ride Safety to set
baseline standards, maintain a national operator registry, mandate third-party
safety audits and insurance, and run a compulsory incident-reporting database
with annual public reporting. This will hopefully ensure minimum safety
protection across States.

SHRI RAJABHAU PARAG PRAKASH WAJE (NASHIK): Thank you, hon.
Chairperson, Madam. I wish to draw the attention the Government to a serious
national security concern regarding the AI-enabled CCTV and traffic
surveillance being installed in Nashik city ahead of the Kumbh Mela, 2027. The
proposed system includes facial recognition, automatic number plate
recognition, AI-based analytics, and centralised command and control
integration. While these technologies are useful for policing and traffic
management, they also create a highly sensitive surveillance infrastructure. If
such systems are compromised through cyber inclusion and unauthorised
access, they could expose real-time information about crowd movement,
security deployment, VVIP roads. This concern becomes critical as millions of
pilgrims, saints and international visitors will gather during the Kumbh Mela,
along with the presence of VVIPs and foreign dignitaries. Any breach or
manipulation of surveillance feeds could pose serious threats to public safety
and national security.
Therefore, I urge the Government to immediately mandate a national-
level cyber security audit of the entire surveillance network in Nashik by
agencies, such as NCIIPC. Conduct independent penetration testing; ensure
that all data servers are securely located within India; prohibit vulnerable
foreign components in critical systems, and stabilise a dedicated cyber

that on the ground level, some gas agencies and distributors are resorting to

*SHRI BALWANT BASWANT WANKHEDE (AMRAVATI): Honorable
Chairperson Madam, my city of Amravati has fallen into the clutches of MD
drugs. Recently, the police administration conducted raids in which MD drugs
worth crores of rupees were seized. The police agency has carried out three or
four such raids; while the trail sometimes points to connections in Ahmedabad,
Gujarat, and at other times to Rajasthan, it is imperative to identify the
mastermind behind this operation. The young people of Amravati city have
become ensnared in the grip of drugs, and the government must take
appropriate measures to rescue them. The government has failed to provide a
satisfactory explanation regarding the exact source of these drugs. However,
the operations conducted in recent times suggest that Amravati may well be
the central hub for this illicit trade, from where these drugs could potentially be
distributed across the entire state of Maharashtra.
Honorable Chairperson Madam, therefore, I demand that both the
Central and State governments appoint a special task force to conduct a
thorough investigation into this matter, take decisive action, and eradicate this
drug menace from its very roots.

JAN VISHWAS (AMENDMENT OF PROVISIONS) BILL, 2026
माननीय अ(cid:197)य (cid:177) : आइटम नंबर 20 A, िजितन (cid:255)साद जी।
आप िबल को इं(cid:367)ोड्यूज क(cid:236)िजए।
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMERCE AND
INDUSTRY; AND MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF
ELECTRONICS AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY (SHRI JITIN
PRASADA): Hon. Speaker Sir, I move for leave to introduce a Bill to amend
certain enactments for decriminalising and rationalising offences to further
enhance trust-based governance for ease of living and doing business.
It seeks to enhance ease of doing business and ease of living by
decriminalising minor offences and implementing measures such as revising
fines and penalties proportionate to the offence, establishing adjudicating
officers and setting up appellate authorities. It proposes to amend 79 Central
Acts administered by 23 Ministries. A total of 784 provisions are being
proposed to be amended, out of which 717 provisions are being decriminalised
to foster ease of doing business, and 67 provisions are being proposed to
facilitate ease of living. This builds on the Jan Vishwas (Amendment of
Provisions) Act, 2023, which decriminalised 183 provisions under 42 Central
Acts, continuing efforts to streamline regulations and promote trust-based
governance.
 Published in the Gazette of India, Extraordinary, Part-II, Section 2, dated 27.03.2026.

Speaker Sir, to resolve this long-standing issue and facilitate the
development of these areas, the State Government of Maharashtra has
proposed three specific alternatives to the Central Government. One of these
proposals suggests that the State Government would pay 25% of the land
value to the Center based on the current Ready Reckoner rates. The
remaining 75% of the land would then be developed by the State Government
as per SRA norms, and 25% of the developed portion would be handed back
to the Central Government. Alternatively, if development on the current site is
not feasible, the Central Government should provide 75% of the land's value to
the State, allowing the State to rehabilitate the slum dwellers at an alternate
location. Furthermore, the State Government is fully prepared to provide
complete cooperation if the Center chooses to develop these lands through its
own agencies, such as the Rail Land Development Authority (RLDA).
However, it is disheartening to note that the Central Government has not yet
provided a proactive or positive response to these proposals. While the intent
to develop the land is clear, such development cannot and should not happen
by displacing or ruining the lives of the people currently living there. These
residents have their schools, livelihoods, and entire social ecosystems rooted
in these locations for decades.

joint meeting with the State Government to find a humanitarian solution that
ensures justice for these residents. We are talking about 2.15 lakh slum
dwellings. A collaborative approach will not only benefit the residents but also

regretted that Punjab floods didn’t find a mention even once during this Budget

unfortunate that despite several written demands for declaring the border road

I have been making efforts since 2007 to provide a permanent irrigation
solution to the people and farmers of drought affected districts of Karnataka
such as Chikkaballapur, Bangalore Rural and Kolar and other Bayaluseeme
(Plateau) districts of Karnnataka.
The previous BJP Government in Karnataka State had announced a
plan to ensure tertiary (third-stage) treated water to the people.
However, this initiative was cancelled by the present Government of
Karnataka as it is discontinued many other projects. Several scientific studies
have indicated that the adverse health among the people is caused by the
water, which is treated only two stages. Therefore, I would like to propose
three suggestions to consider in this regard.
A scientific guidelines issued by the Union government should be
implemented by the state government to ensure the water is treated at tertiary
level (third-stage) before it is released. And, the Yettinahole project works
should be expedited and completed at the earliest.
The allocation of 15 TMC of water share from the river Krishna should
be released to mitigate the water scarcity and save the precious lives of the
people of these districts.
Thanking you.

DR. MALLU RAVI (NAGARKURNOOL): Thank you very much, hon.
Chairperson Madam, for giving me an opportunity to speak about my
parliamentary constituency, Nagarkurnool.
Madam, I come from a very backward parliamentary constituency, and
there are no MSMEs or heavy industries in Nagarkurnool. It is very much
neglected in the field of MSMEs and heavy industries.
Madam, unemployment is increasing significantly in my parliamentary
constituency. Previous history shows that many of the youth went into Maoist
activities, and now, that problem has come under control because there has
been some improvement in the irrigation sector.
Through you, Madam Chairperson, I would request the hon. Finance
Minister to take up Nagarkurnool parliamentary constituency as a model
constituency where she can give direction to all the banks to promote MSMEs,
so that small and vulnerable sections of the society can start these MSMEs
and get employment, and also generate employment for others.
Also, through you, Madam Chairperson, I request the Minister of Heavy
Industries to undertake a special study of the Nagarkurnool parliamentary
constituency and try to establish some heavy industries there. Otherwise, he
may also direct the heavy industries that are there in Hyderabad to have

*SHRI BAJRANG MANOHAR SONWANE (BEED): Honourable Chairperson, I
rise to present the plight of hundreds of thousands of farmers from the Beed
district in the Marathwada region of Maharashtra. Millions of farmers across
Maharashtra—and indeed the vast majority of farmers in the Beed district—are
currently enduring the severe hardships inflicted by drought. However, the
situation today has become truly dire. On one hand, there is drought; on the
other, excessive rainfall, unseasonal showers, and erratic weather—factors
that can obliterate a farmer's entire year's worth of hard work in a mere instant.
This is not merely a natural calamity; it constitutes a grave injustice being
inflicted upon the farming community. Whether facing 'celestial' crises (natural
disasters) or 'earthly' crises (administrative and systemic hardships), farmers
find themselves relentlessly besieged on all fronts. Consequently, burdened by
insurmountable debt, many farmers are driven to the tragic act of suicide.
Hon. Chairperson, given the prevailing drought conditions in my home
district of Beed, there is an urgent and critical need for water. To address this
requirement, the government had previously initiated a 'River-Linking Project'
designed to divert water from the Ujani Dam in Solapur district to my district of
* English translation of the speech originally delivered in Marathi.

the demand that this financial assistance be made available to them without
further delay.

which SC beneficiaries receive by virtue of eligibility, such as occupation,

designed to address historical disadvantage and structural inequities.
To illustrate, I would like to draw the attention of the House to the
allocation under PM-KISAN. In the Financial Year 2026-27, the scheme has a
total outlay of approximately Rs. 63,500 crore, of which Rs. 11,707 crore has

allocation. However, the beneficiary data suggests that, out of approximately

appear progressive on paper, it is important to note that SC farmers receive
benefits by virtue of being farmers, rather than due to any SC-specific targeting
within the scheme. This raises an important concern. Allocations classified
under the SCSP may, in certain cases, represent not additional welfare, but
rather an accounting attribution of benefits that would have accrued
irrespective of social category. This could dilute the core intent of the Sub-
Plan, which is to deliver incremental and targeted gains for the disadvantaged
groups. In light of this, I humbly submit the following considerations for
strengthening the SCSP framework. … (Interruptions)

immense importance to our farmers. I wish to bring to the attention of this

*ADV. GOWAAL KAGADA PADAVI (NANDURBAR): Honorable Chairperson
Madam, thank you. My parliamentary constituency of Nandurbar is recognized
as the number one district in the entire state of Maharashtra for papaya
production. However, despite such large-scale production, farmers still do not
receive fair prices for their produce. Through you, I would like to urge the
Central Government to establish an independent 'Papaya processing Park' in
my Nandurbar constituency. This park should be equipped with facilities for
papaya grading, washing, packaging, and storage. Furthermore, Nandurbar
should be included under the 'One Nation, One Product' scheme to garner
both national and international recognition. Financial assistance should be
extended to papaya-growing farmers through initiatives such as the PM Kisan
Sampada Scheme, the Mega Food Park Scheme, and APEDA. Additionally, a
skill development and training center should be established for tribal youth—
both young men and women—to generate local employment opportunities.
Cold storage facilities and logistics centers should also be set up within the
district. Hon. Madam, if this Papaya Park is established, it will benefit
thousands of farmers; their incomes will double, they will receive fair
remuneration for their produce, and their agricultural produce will no longer go
to waste. Moreover, market control will no longer remain solely in the hands of
traders, and the Papaya Park will accord Nandurbar recognition on a national
level. Therefore, I appeal to the Central Government to grant approval for this

Madam Chairperson, the Mithila region is witnessing all-round efforts
made by the Government for expeditious development works completed and
undertaken under the leadership of the PM. The site for consecrating the piece
of pious and traditionally important land at Ayodhya was taken up and
completed at Ramjanmabhoomi Tirthakshetra, Ayodhya and now people from
all around the world throng there for worship and prayer along with annual
sacraments. On the same line, Madam, a temple has been constructed at a
cost of Rupees 850 crore in Sitamarhi, Bihar for besetting the female deity
Goddess Sita, the all-time-adored daughter of Mithila.
Madam, the day is celebrated as an epoch-old festival of RANAVAMI-a
cult in prevalence throughout the country. I am grateful to the hon’ble Home
Minister Shri Amit Bhai Shah for extending support for the sacrament. I am
also grateful to the Prime Minister for setting up of Makhana Board; providing
GI tagging for Makhana-the fox nut; releasing a postal-stamp of Mithila-Paag;
renovation and upgradation of Darbhanga Airport; construction of an IT park,
releasing an amount of 11,500 crore rupees for solving the recurring annual
flood in the region and an amount of 6,500 crore rupees for raising the height
of both the embankments of the Dam on Koshi river.
Madam, I would like to raise the issues pertaining the region as well as
the state that industrialization has been overlooked during the tenure of

*SHRI SUKANTA KUMAR PANIGRAHI (KANDHAMAL): Thank you,
Chairperson Madam. Today, I wish to express about an important matter
regarding my constituency. For the last 30 years, the survey work for our
Gopalpur – Rairakhol railway line has been conducted repeatedly, and even
now, ORIDL (Odisha Rail Infrastructure Development Ltd) has already
submitted its report to the Government.
However, it is a matter of great concern that this railway line, which
connects South Odisha with West Odisha via Kandhamal, remains an absolute
necessity but remained untouched till date. My parliamentary constituency is a
tribal-dominant area and an aspirational district; to this day, it remains the only
district in Odisha where the district headquarters has not been connected by a
railway line—that is Kandhamal district.
Therefore, through you, I would like to appeal to the Government to
ensure that the Gopalpur – Rairakhol railway line is connected as soon as
possible.This project should be completed to ensure the economic progress
and livelihood of the countless tribal brothers, sisters, and people from
